prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original Sugata artist discussion sheet, one static image containing three equal portrait panels.
Input image 1: identity and presentation reference only, not an edit target. Use the clearly adult fictional man in the larger right-hand portrait of the reference: the same warm medium-brown skin, dark-brown eyes, straight nose, full lips, jaw shape, short dark swept hair and subtle beard shadow. Preserve the olive pointed-collar overshirt over an ivory crew-neck tee. Do not redraw the reference's full-body/portrait layout.
Scene and style: a refined realistic character-development portrait sheet with natural skin texture, soft grey studio background and consistent soft studio lighting. One landscape canvas, three evenly sized separated columns, one head-and-shoulders portrait per column. All three show the same adult character at matching camera distance, lens perspective, face scale and shoulder crop. Keep the whole hair crown, both brows, both eyes, nose and mouth readable in every panel. Keep identical hair, wardrobe, skin material, exposure and background across panels.
Left panel — neutral design baseline: head upright and facing the viewer, eyes looking directly at the viewer, both eyebrows resting evenly, relaxed lips closed without a smile, relaxed nose and cheeks.
Middle panel — a gentle playful-teasing artist intention: mostly frontal head with a slight tilt, eyes directly toward the viewer, a small symmetric closed-lip smile, a mild lift of one eyebrow while the other stays relaxed. Both eyes remain clearly open and readable; keep the nose relaxed. The expression should be restrained and natural.
Right panel — a reserved sideways-coy artist intention: head turned slightly to the side with chin modestly lowered; eyes return toward the viewer; a small symmetric relaxed closed-lip smile, relaxed brows and nose. Keep both eyes and brows visible; the intentional head-and-gaze relationship is the main difference from the middle panel.
Constraints: exactly three coherent portraits of the same clearly adult fictional identity. No teeth showing, nose wrinkle, one-sided upper-lip lift, hard squint, grimace or theatrical exaggeration. No extra subjects, props, jewellery, hats, glasses, text, panel labels, logos or watermark. No hair hiding a brow or eye. This is newly authored static art using the original character as a reference; it is not a scientific emotion-recognition illustration or a rig/control demonstration.
